findings.reason: the §4 design should name `_GitHubClient` (catalog_release.py:58) as the owner to extend and route the refusal comment through it, so the package keeps one authority for pull-request writes instead of two that can drift in auth, error shape and retry posture.
findings.text: the fold-back refusal is posted via a new `_pull_request_comment` that delegates to `imas_codex.graph.ghcr.github_api_call`, creating a second pull-request REST write path beside `_GitHubClient` in imas_codex/standard_names/catalog_release.py:58, whose own docstring declares it "The single pull-request boundary; every call goes over GitHub REST" and which already owns the write direction (`create_pull_request` at :74, `update_pull_request_body`), with a second error renderer (`github_error_detail`) beside that module's `_rest_error_detail`; a reviewer-facing write should extend that owner with a comment method, not fork a parallel boundary

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the remaining deliverable is wiring over existing machinery, not a new module; `notify_refusal_on_pull_request` (promote.py:1524) hides URL parsing, notice rendering and transport-failure handling behind one boolean return, and the traceability path reuses the dedicated writer at promote.py:1627 rather than adding a parallel one.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the deliverable-three write posts onto the pull request through a second REST boundary in `promote.py` rather than extending the boundary the package already declares as authoritative, `_GitHubClient` in `imas_codex/standard_names/catalog_release.py`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — supplied figures public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the design adds no CLI option, no MCP view and no public entry point beyond two module-level helpers in `promote.py`, so no section adds to any of the four families without accounting for it. (The already-landed refusal-notice helpers `refusal_notice_body`/`notify_refusal_on_pull_request` are the only named public additions and both live inside the one section whose text states it is closing the sole missing capability; no section retires anything because nothing in these families is added.)
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan carries two reuse maps (17 candidates, 17 verdicts, §4a; and 13 capability rows, 44/44 citations verified at base, §4) and the claims check out: `_require_matching_graph_target` (imas_codex/cli/graph/data.py:155) is genuinely reused by all three destructive callers (data.py:663 load, :1405 clear, registry.py:1163 pull), and the approval/traceability writers it names (`mark_catalog_name_approved`, `undo_approval`) exist and are extended rather than rebuilt.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one new wrapper, `_pull_request_comment` (promote.py:1466), is justified in the section text (§4 comment c-20260917-providers-for-the-remaining-deliverables): the plan states exactly one capability lacks a provider and that the transport beneath it is reusable, so the wrapper is a named, minimal seam over `github_api_call` rather than an unjustified layer. Its width problem is a duplicate-ownership problem, reported below.
